source.title: Bayesian Deep Learning and a Probabilistic Perspective of Generalization

page_placements.theme: Arbitrary-label fitting extends beyond standard deep networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests fitting random labels with Gaussian processes and a Bayesian neural network, using the original intervention but a different model and inference method.
record.gate_note: Own results include GP accuracy on random and true labels, BNN training accuracy on fully corrupted labels, and marginal-likelihood trends as label corruption increases. Other discussion of Zhang et al. is cited prior work and is not recorded as a result.
record.test_reason: The PreResNet-20 experiment directly measures perfect fitting of fully randomized CIFAR-10 labels in a Bayesian analysis setting. The GP experiments use a model class outside V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors reproduce random-label interpolation with GPs and interpret decreasing approximate marginal likelihood under corruption as evidence of useful inductive biases despite broad support. They do not dispute neural networks' ability to fit random labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GP regression/classification and Bayesian neural networks with approximate inference to examine random-label fitting and marginal likelihood, rather than reproducing the original standard SGD experiment unchanged.
record.method_sensitivity: For the BNN random-label fitting experiment, weight decay and data augmentation are turned off and the initial learning rate is lowered to 0.01.

fits_no_version.finding: The ten-class RBF GP achieves 100% training accuracy and 10.4% test accuracy on random labels; on true labels it achieves 72.8% training and 54.3% test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RBF Gaussian processes can interpolate randomized image labels while generalizing above chance when trained on true labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Approximate marginal likelihood decreases with increasing label corruption for the binary GP and PreResNet-20 experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These approximate Bayesian evidence calculations favor less corrupted CIFAR-10 datasets despite the models' ability to fit randomized labels.

record.problems: The random-label BNN fitting setup changes weight decay, data augmentation, and learning rate; the text does not report its test accuracy on random labels. Marginal-likelihood trends are described without numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible random-label results identified. Numeric values for the marginal-likelihood curves in Figure 7(d,e) are not recoverable from the supplied text; the stated trends are recorded in R5–R6.

untested.parts: Random-label test performance is not stated numerically for PreResNet-20. Fitting with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to a true-label baseline is not established; the experiment disables weight decay and augmentation and lowers the learning rate.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit at every intermediate corruption fraction and steadily increasing test error toward chance are not established by the readable results.

Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them preserves true-label generalization. Disabling regularizers without a controlled comparison does not test these propositions.
The order in which real patterns and noisy labels are learned during training.

missing.what: Figure 7(e) includes a test-error axis alongside marginal likelihood across label-corruption levels, but no row records the test-error series. Its values and trend cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text rendering.

record.verdict_notes: Changed training settings and unreported outcomes are coverage limitations, not demonstrated failures warranting limits_scope. The GP findings challenge an interpretation that random-label fitting is unique to neural networks; none of the supplied versions asserts that uniqueness.

versions.untested_parts: For the BNN, the text does not report test accuracy on random labels or true-label generalization. The BNN setup turns off weight decay and data augmentation and uses a lower initial learning rate, so it does not test the unchanged-hyperparameters condition. GP results are a different model class.
The text reports marginal-likelihood trends as corruption increases, but does not report test error rising steadily or perfect training fit across the corruption fractions.
